metadata.display_heading: THE MAJOR GOALS OF QUANTITATIVE GENETICS / The Estimation of Breeding Values
metadata.source_title: Genetics and Analysis of Quantitative Traits

blocks.content: Plant and animal breeding programs are based on the principle that an individual's phenotype provides some insight into its underlying genotypic value. However, because the environment can contribute greatly to phenotypic expression, the amount of genetic information conveyed by a single phenotypic measurement is not necessarily high. On the other hand, if one considers jointly the phenotypes of all of the relatives of a focal individual, a more accurate assessment of that individual's breeding value can be acquired. The identification of elite individuals by BLUP (Chapter 26), in some cases supplemented by information from molecular markers, is now a major goal of applied quantitative genetics.
